name: HTML5 FileSystem
location: Chrome: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\<Profile>\File System ; Edge: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\<Profile>\File System (Chromium browsers only; not implemented by Firefox)
purpose: Implements the HTML5 local storage FileSystem API, letting web applications store larger binary data locally than the 10MB text-only limit of HTML5 Web Storage allows.
key_fields: LevelDB index database (maps visited URLs to assigned subfolders)
normal_baseline: Populated by web apps the user actively uses for offline functionality (webmail attachment caches, offline-capable SaaS tools, progressive web apps).
anomalies: File System storage tied to a domain absent from browsing History
Binary content in a "p" (permanent) subfolder resembling executables, scripts, or archives rather than typical web app cache data
Recently modified File System data timestamped within a known compromise window
parsing_tools: ccl_chrome_indexeddb (CCL / obsidianforensics: includes a FileSystem API module)
anti_forensic_notes: Clearing "site data" in browser settings removes File System storage for that origin; because it is a lesser-known storage mechanism, it is less commonly targeted for anti-forensic cleanup than history or cookies and can retain data longer as a result.
interpretation: A LevelDB database within the File System folder maps visited URLs/origins to the numbered subfolders that actually hold the stored files. Data splits between "t" (temporary, browser-managed, evictable) and "p" (permanent, explicitly requested by the site) storage. Content in permanent storage reflects a more deliberate site action and is generally more forensically interesting.
